key_insight: The paper extends high-order curvilinear finite-element Lagrangian hydrodynamics to an implicit time-integration framework without changing the underlying physics or spatial discretization.
engineering_relevance: This enables larger stable time steps for challenging shock-driven flows, improving accuracy-per-time-to-solution for high-order solid/fluid mechanics simulations.
method: Builds an implicit solver on the existing Laghos/MFEM explicit formulation and preserves the original operator structure.
Uses MFEM $\partial$FEM plus Enzyme automatic differentiation to form Jacobian actions for Newton-Krylov solves in matrix-free or assembled mode.
Introduces smooth artificial viscosity to make shock handling differentiable and compatible with gradient-based nonlinear solvers.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on standard benchmarks: high-order convergence for Taylor-Green vortex, correct strong-shock behavior on Sedov blast, and improved accuracy-per-time-to-solution on the Triple Point problem.
watch_item: The current differentiable artificial viscosity does not include a limiter, so high-order scaling away from shocks is not yet fully guaranteed.
paper_title: Implicit Lagrangian Hydrodynamics with High-Order Finite Elements
